courses.title: Not many people can time the stock market so most folks try to increase their time in the market. For that approach to be successful, picking the right set of securities is key. (Length: 60 minutes)
courses.description: You have watched our previous courses on this subject and feel ready to trade. Now, it is time to find the right security to trade! In this course, we will go over a few methodologies you could follow to help you pick the right stock to trade given both micro and macro economic conditions. There are numerous ways to skin this cat so we will look at a few approaches that have worked well for us.

descriptions: This session teaches a structured way to find trading candidates. Starting with brokerage platforms, paper trading, and watchlists, you will pick tickers from industries you know such as food, tech, finance before branching out. You will compare peers by price and behavior, see how stocks track sectors, and balance diversification with risk. Examples span semiconductors, restaurants, and banks, showing why portfolio balance matters across time horizons. Earnings take center stage: how EPS, revenue, guidance, and sentiment drive swings, why after hours differs, and how markets often react unexpectedly to reports.

The lessons covers key metrics such as P/E and forward P/E to spot growth versus maturity, EPS trends, short interest, 52 week ranges, and liquidity as a gauge of volatility and tradability. You will see why percentage moves matter more than dollar moves. Tools are explored through hands on practice with brokerage platforms, Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha, TipRanks, and YCharts, with emphasis on cross-checking data. Finally, you will turn research into decisions: define entries and exits, respect stops, and size positions wisely while weighing macro, micro, and thematic drivers to balance risk and reward.

courses.name: Basics of Product Management
courses.title: Are you a Software Developer looking to become a Product Manager? Or, a new graduate who is interested in Product Management as a career? (Length: 50 minutes)
courses.description: This course should help you get a head start on some of the basics of managing software products at work. The example we will go over is a real one, and is based on one of our current apps (snowpal.com) which is a Project Management platform.

descriptions: This course introduces product management through a real world example: designing a Kanban board for our web app. Instead of abstract frameworks, you will act as if the feature does not exist and follow the PM process of defining, discussing, and structuring it with engineering teams. You will see how PMs validate needs, set scope, and align with designers and API teams, focusing on clarity and fast execution. Then you will break requirements into smaller parts such as buttons, lists, renaming, and archiving while separating core features, UI/UX, and backend work for iterative delivery and feedback.

The course highlights collaboration between product and engineering, showing how developers ask practical questions like whether a list appears instantly or after server confirmation and how PMs focus on outcomes to clear ambiguity. You will see prioritization in action: resisting the urge to ship every feature upfront and instead starting with a streamlined release. Advanced features like relations or cross block moves are deferred until later, guided by user feedback. By the end, you will understand how PMs turn vague ideas into buildable features through clarity, communication, and iteration.

courses.name: Day Trading Stocks: Part 1
courses.title: Day Trading is not for everyone. But if you are the kind of person who might enjoy it, there are a few things you would likely be better off knowing. (Length: 65 minutes)
courses.description: In this course, we will explore a few different facets of Day Trading, and see if we can potentially find some lucrative approaches. While the course will focus on US Equities, the underlying fundamentals should be applicable no matter where you live, and trade.

descriptions: This course introduces day trading with a focus on U.S. equities while keeping lessons global. You will learn what day trading is, how FINRA defines pattern day traders, and why rules matter. Short term trading across a few days is also covered, showing where strategies overlap. The course explores today’s day trading landscape, covering demographics, success rates, and attrition to reveal why few remain profitable long term. With that context, you will examine motivations, from side income to full time pursuits, and weigh them against risk, resilience, and lifestyle fit with candid guidance and real anecdotes.

The course tackles the risks of day trading, showing how a 6.5 hour window magnifies volatility, why reversals can erase gains, and how margin increases exposure. Stress, speed, and potential losses are central themes. You will also get a practical view of infrastructure including opening accounts, margin rules, capital allocation, interest, margin calls, and taxes such as short term gains and wash sale rules. Finally, the course reviews habits and order types, from market versus limit to long versus short, while emphasizing house rules, position sizing, and discipline as keys to realistic success.

courses.name: Day Trading Stocks: Part 2
courses.title: In the last course, we discussed some of the fundamentals of day trading. We will pick up from where we left off, and continue to delve a little deeper into it. (Length: 58 minutes)
courses.description: As a follow up to the previous course, we will look at some of the steps involved in picking securities to trade during the course of a given day. How should we go about doing it, what should we be looking at, and more.

descriptions: This course builds on Day Trading Part 1 and focuses on executing trades. It assumes familiarity with the basics and emphasizes repeatable habits for selecting and managing securities within a single day. You will learn to break the 6.5 hour U.S. session into phases: observe early, trade mid day, and exit before close, creating structure and discipline. The course also covers how to choose securities by industry, volatility, or market cap, while weighing concentration against diversification. Real examples illustrate how news, earnings, or events can shift focus and why flexibility is essential when sentiment changes quickly.

The course covers tools and monitoring, from using Seeking Alpha to track industries to setting alerts for price moves. You will compare active watching with automation and see how each fits different trading styles. Risk management is central, including deciding on long or short trades, allocating capital, and setting stop losses by percentage or dollar value, while noting why stops may fail in volatile markets. You will also learn to size trades wisely and understand tax impacts such as short term gains and wash sale rules. The course closes with flexibility, showing how to adapt strategies to news, earnings, and events.

courses.name: 36 Ways AI Is Rewriting Work as We Know It
courses.title: The End of Work (as you knew it). You are not ready for what AI is about to do to your job. This course can serve as a field guide to the AI Era. (Length: 110 minutes)
courses.description: AI is reshaping every layer of work—from roles and team composition to workflows, education, and organizational structures. It massively boosts efficiency but also forces companies and individuals to adapt quickly.

descriptions: What if everything you believed about work, teams, and learning was about to be shattered almost overnight? AI is not just boosting productivity, it is rewriting the rules. Solo developers are building billion-dollar companies. Non-coders are creating software in hours. Teams are shrinking, roles are dissolving, and busywork is being eliminated. The very definition of what counts as valuable skills is being rewritten in real time. Departments are blending into one another. Change is accelerating at breakneck speed. And as machines learn to reason, the frontier of work itself is shifting. The truth is that we are not moving fast enough.

Step into the rapidly evolving world of AI-driven work. This course explores how artificial intelligence is transforming teams, roles, and workflows at unprecedented speed. From solo developers creating billion-dollar startups to non-coders releasing software in just hours, AI is changing the way we work by boosting productivity and reducing repetitive tasks. Participants will examine the skills that truly matter in this new landscape, such as reasoning, creativity, and judgment, while learning how to leverage AI tools, adapt to shifting organizational structures, and thrive in a world where change is the only constant. AI massively boosts efficiency but also forces companies and individuals to adapt quickly.
